<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to identify correct description. Let's inspect details:

The article states:

: "In this paper, we present WizardMath, which enhances the mathematical reasoning ability... We apply the Evol-Instruct method to generate diverse math instructions data by math-specific Evol-Instruct. Then train instruction reward model (IRM) and process-supervised reward model (PRM). They use SFT with data from GSM8k and MATH and also open-domain conversations. They use ChatGPT and Wizard-E for reward supervision. Step 2-3: They train IRM and PRM using external data: they use ChatGPT and Wizard-E to generate instructions, reward. RLE may rely on external reward models; yes, they rely on ChatGPT for supervision. So Step 2-3 cannot be performed without external models. So B is false.

Option A: "In the data construction process of this article, only the training sets of GSM8k and MATH were used as seed datasets, and then the Evolution Instruction method was used to augment the constructed training data." They do use GSM8k and MATH as phase; they also use open-domain conversations from WizardLM training data. So "only the training sets of GSM8k and MATH were used as seed datasets, and with Evol Instruct to augment" is partially true but they also used open-domain? The article says: "To make the parsing of each step easier, we few-shot re-generate 15k answers for GSM8k and MATH with an Alpha version of WizardLM 70B model to produce solutions in a step-by-step format, then find out those with a correct answer, and use this existing data for SFT. To enhance the model’s ability to adhere to the neural and diverse instructions, we also sample 1.5k open-domain conversations from WizardLM’s training data, then merge it with above math corpus as the final SFT training data."

Thus data construction not solely GSM8k and MATH training sets: they also include open domain 1.5k. So A includes "only the training sets… used as seed datasets" but they did create additional. But maybe they were used as seed to produce more instructions, but still they used open domain. So option A maybe inaccurate, maybe it's not correct (since chloride says only training sets used). So A might be false.

Option C: "WizardMath models of all sizes have achieved mathematical abilities that exceed those of partially identical/larger closed source models." The article says in Table 1, WizardGPT 70B surpasses some closed source models like ChatGPT, Claude Instant, PaLM 2 on GSM8k, etc. It surpasses some but not all. The description says "exceed those of partially identical-larger closed source models" which may be vague. It says models of all sizes have achieved mathematical abilities exceeding those of partially identical/larger closed source models. Based on results, 13B surpasses some large closed resources like LR? Table shows 13B surpasses PaLM 1.185? But 13B surpasses PaLM 1(540B) in GSM8k; Actually, 13B surpasses PaLM 1.54? "Closed-source models: GPT-4 [3] - 92.0; ??? but it shows " GPT-4 [3] - 92.0 MATH ??? but no.

But the gist: They highlight that WizardMath 70B surpasses ChatGPT, Claude Instant, PaLM 2 on GSM8k and surpasses Text-davinci-002, PaLM 1, GPT-3 at P@1. So for some closed source models, Wizards exceed.

But description says "of all sizes have achieved mathematical abilities that exceed those of partially identical/larger closed source models." The phrase "partially identical/larger closed source models" claims that they exceed even those that be partially identical/ larger of closed source. This probably correct referencing "WizardMath surpasses all other open source models by a substantial margin" used, but also "surpasses ChatGPT-3, Claude Instant, PaLM 2 on GSM8k" which are closed source. So yes they exceed partially identical closed source models (depending).

Check description D: "This article uses different methods to ensure that no harmful content is generated as much as possible." Does article mention methods to enforce safe content? There's a brief mention of "Wizards separated safe content to produce harmful content." At the end of story, not clearly emphasized. The article may mention safe content and mention they are working with legal team. There is a brief mention "We are working with our legal team to review and publicly release under policy ... The model can provide harmful content." Actually the policy mentions that they work to review safety content, and they might filter or safe-harness. But the article does not elaborate no safe approach. The article says "Wizards LM safety scaffolds." The presence of such maybe no. Another part: "Future work" mention safety guidelines. But not mention methods for harmful content. There is a 'Broader Impact' note: "Similar to the other LLMs ... may generate unethical or harmful information." So article acknowledges but not offering method. So D seems not correct.

Thus which option(s) correct? Let's analyze each:

A: Only GSM8k and MATH training sets used as seed datasets, then extend with Evol-Instruct. Actually they included open domain conversations, 1.5k. So A is partly false. So D? But B is false as well. C might be correct. Let's analyze: "WizardMath models of all sizes have achieved mathematical abilities that exceed those of partially identical/larger closed source models." The article says "WizardMath surpasses all other open-source LLMs by large margin; WizardMath 70B surpassed some closed-source like ChatGPT, Claude Instant, PaLM 2. WizardMath 13B surpasses PaLM 1. So yes maybe they exceed some closed types (ChatGPT and Claude). Provide evidence: "WizardMath 70B surpasses all closed source on GSM8k." Wait "WizardMath 70B slightly outperforms some closed-source LLMs on GSM8k, including ChatGPT, Claude Instant and PaLM 2 540B???". So yes they surpassed some closed. So statement: They exceed those of partially identical/larger closed source models. 70B is similar parameter to those? The article states "WizardMath 70B achieve similar to PaLM 2 (540B) but outruns them." So partially identical/larger: telling that they exceeded some closed source models that in size maybe bigger. But "partially identical/larger" ambiguous. But likely correct as they outperformed some open and some closed. So I'd pick C.
